Here at the edge of Chu Ye's wild, mysterious forest, old festivals are honored even as old wounds fester. Strangers' footsteps are watched, and secrets settle thick as mist along the water's edge.

The town sits at a junction of rivers—once a thriving logging and mining hub, now a skeleton of its former self. The closest shore leads north to the sea; the rivers join together into a large lake to the east.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Willowshore had a heyday long ago, but those days are past. The old industries collapsed, and the population dwindled. For generations, the village was too small and poor to warrant attention from Shogun Tsuneni's regime. In the oni's absence, a local family rose to become de facto rulers.

Now, after generations without an oni mayor, one is finally arriving—claiming to have "always been here." This has stirred unrest and reopened old divisions.

docs.title: The Revival of Friendship
docs.text:
A traditional rite observed at every change of power—whether a new store manager or a new mayor—where old grudges are publicly put to rest. It serves as an unofficial but very customary Transfer of Power.

The ruling family is refusing to participate in the ceremony for the new oni mayor. This defiance has created tension throughout the village.

docs.title: Festival of Returning Spirits
docs.text: An ancient festival held on the eve of autumn, meant to protect Willowshore from whatever haunts the dark woods beyond. The whole town gathers as lanterns flicker and drums thrum. Participants are chosen to lead a ceremonial play, walking in the shadows as the founders once did—acting out the fragile bargain that keeps the unknown at bay.

docs.title: The Rite of Open Reckoning
docs.text:
Not a Willowshore tradition but a Chu Ye imperial legal procedure that was invoked here by Magistrate Kurosawa during Session 8. It is an open court hearing: the accused are tried publicly in front of the whole town. Anyone holding public office may invoke the Rite. A judge—typically the highest local authority—hears the evidence, and the judge's ruling is final. The crowd does not vote; they witness.

Both prosecution and defense may call witnesses. The accused may speak in their own defense. The Rite is rarely invoked in modern practice, and carries weight precisely because of its severity.

In the party's case, the mayor served as judge. The verdict was guilty.

docs.title: The Forest Story
docs.text:
The oldest story villagers whisper about the forest shadows involves will-o-wisps that lead people astray into the woods.

Why no one speaks the ending:

The story's ending is never told aloud—not because it's forgotten, but because no one can agree on it, and speaking it starts fights. The disagreement runs deep, touching on old loyalties and resentments.

The truth, known to few: The ending embarrasses the ruling family. The heir to the family fortune was said to have been "lured away by forest spirits." In reality, he simply got drunk and wandered into the woods. His father—a teetotaler—spun the tale about spirits to save face.

This deception created factions. Some people secretly blame each other; some welcomed the oni as a chance to unseat the old rulers. One member of the ruling family (The Smiling One) whispers when they think no one is listening: "I know the real ending."

docs.title: Local Customs
docs.text:
• Averting eyes from oni: When oni enter town, lower classes must avert their gaze—only the ruling class may look upon them
  • "I've always been here": The official stance that oni have always been present, despite obvious evidence otherwise
  • Spirit death rituals: Local legend holds that death near a spirit requires special disposal of the body, lest it return or be controlled

docs.title: The Spirit of Willowshore
docs.text:
GM retcon (post–Session Fourteen)

Established by Gary's post-session note: Tian Xia has an active spirit realm, and the folk of Chu Ye know it. Spirits are real, present, and interacted with — a fisherman may seek help from the river spirit as a matter of course. The characters have always known this, even where the players didn't.

Willowshore, like the grove and the river, has a spirit of its own. The Grandmother — herself a nature spirit of the Hollow of Seven Cedars, cast into service long ago — left the party a seed that clears the memory-curse from whoever consumes it. Fed to one person, it cures one person (half went to Radiant Willow). But offered to the town spirit of Willowshore — if the party can learn to commune with it and earn its favor — the spirit could consume the seed and cleanse the entire town.

The spirit now has a name: Old Amber (identified Session Fifteen) — the river spirit of Willowshore's waters, an old amber-gold koi, once appeased with rice offerings on full moons and festival nights. It was silent for roughly two years — since before the oni arrived — and most of the old town believed it abandoned them. The truth (Session Sixteen): it had been imprisoned in the Land of Dreams, in a ward of five lanterns guarded by the Mother of a Thousand Wings.

docs.title: The Curse Lifted (Session Sixteen)
docs.text:
The party tore the ward apart from inside the dream, and Old Amber — free — ate the last half of the seed. The effect reached the waking town within moments:

  • Every person in Willowshore was cured at once. They remember everything they did and felt under the curse — Yong and Hong remember their feud — but their feelings are their own again. The town understood immediately that its mind had been "enchanted... somehow manipulated"
  • The river accelerated, as if the spirit were dragging the curse downstream and dissolving it into nothing. Fishermen shouted as fish leapt into their nets; the water turned brighter; the reeds along the shoreline bloomed. "A painting that has gone from dark to light — like turning a page"
  • The town began speaking of it at once: Old Amber has blessed us; the river spirit's favor is won; whatever cursed the town is over. The Silver Mist Inn filled up. Strangers bought the party drinks. Willow called a festival for that evening to celebrate the spirit's return
  • The Rite of Open Reckoning's legitimacy collapsed with the curse: the townsfolk who testified against the party now apologize for it, and Mayor Masru surrendered Kurosawa's handwritten verdict script for the first trial

docs.title: The Second Curse
docs.text: Old Amber's parting words established that the town's trouble is not over. Beneath the memory curse Kurosawa built runs something older and colder — "not part of the first" — that "moves the way grief moves through a family that stops speaking of it. Quiet in the day. Patient. It has learned to keep a door for itself, and to smile from behind it." It likely predates the oni and likely silenced Old Amber two years ago. The party's first suspect is Cheng Yesho, the Smiling One — and the ruling family he belongs to.

docs.title: Notable Locations
docs.text: Location Description The Yeshou Estate Former manor of the ruling family; now occupied by Magistrate Kurosawa The Torii Gate Traditional gate at the bridge crossing The Graveyard Cemetery with family plots, shrines, and cricket cages near the Dark Woods edge The River Site of strange occurrences; where Ginkgo and Da Baishan witnessed a spirit killing Eternal Blaze Ironworks Blacksmith shop run by Yong, a young kitsune Silver Mist Lodge Once-grand inn on the riverside; where the ruling family is temporarily staying Dew Drop Petals Salon and spa run by Radiant Willow Cloud Paper Lodge Paper lantern shop; their fireworks were stored in the warehouse Seven Colored Songbird Theater Open-air theater north of the bridge; site of performances, ceremonies, and the Festival of Returning Spirits transfer of power Liwen's Flower Cart Tiny florist shop (barely more than a cart) run by Liwen Luda's Shop Seamstress and informal arcane supplier run by Luda; deals in rare plants, alchemy ingredients, and spell components The Luckless Cod Local tavern where workers drink after hours The Warehouse Dock storage for festival fireworks; partially destroyed by fire The Dark Woods Dense forest to the north; home of the Mourndusk Willow; dangerous at night

docs.title: Oni Regime
docs.text:
• Magistrate Kurosawa — Blue-skinned oni magistrate enforcing martial law
  • Mayor Masru — The affable blue-skinned oni mayor, now in residence
  • Four red-skinned oni guards in samurai armor

docs.title: Residents
docs.text:
• Mido — Matriarch of the Yeshou family
  • The Smiling One — Ruling family member who "knows the real ending"
  • Donkey — Ancient elf wizard; village witch
  • Yong — Kitsune blacksmith at Eternal Blaze Ironworks
  • Hong — Yong's son; hired to set the warehouse fire
  • Radiant Willow — Flower leshy beautician at Dew Drop Petals

docs.title: Visitors
docs.text:
• Da Baishan — Orc investigator drawn by suspicion of the oni
  • Boone — Dwarf fighter from distant lands
  • Ginkgo — Fungus leshy cleric gathering information
  • Littlefinger — Halfling rogue with ties to the ruling family
  • Cassian Voss — (deceased) Researcher from Absalom who studied "old gods"; now an untethered spirit

docs.title: Session Zero (2026-01-16)
docs.text:
• Village established as the campaign's starting location
  • World-building created the Revival of Friendship tradition
  • The forest story and its forbidden ending established
  • "The Smiling One" created as a mystery NPC
  • The torii gate, bridge, and river featured in character bonds

docs.title: Session One (2026-01-30)
docs.text:
• Magistrate Kurosawa introduced as the advance guard for the mayor
  • The ruling family displaced from their estate to Silver Mist Lodge
  • A warehouse fire destroyed many festival preparations; children rescued by the party
  • Multiple new locations discovered and visited by the party

docs.title: Session Two (2026-02-05)
docs.text:
• Hong revealed as the arsonist, hired by the Yeshou family
  • Mido introduced as the family matriarch; admitted to the sabotage and canceled further plans
  • Kurosawa's secret visits to the Mourndusk Willow in the Dark Woods revealed
  • Undead rose in the graveyard for the first time in living memory
  • The party fought a ghoul, a zombie, and an undead cat at the cemetery
  • A spirit connected to Ginkgo and Da Baishan's secret appeared during and after combat
  • Yong planning to leave Willowshore; "sees dark skies ahead"

docs.title: Session Three (2026-02-12)
docs.text:
• The party explored the Dark Woods and discovered a dark summoning ritual at the Mourndusk Willow
  • The river spirit identified as Cassian Voss, a foreign researcher from Absalom
  • Fought blight-infected wildlife at the Mourndusk Willow; Ginkgo created a salve to cleanse the lichen blight
  • Mido identified the ritual as a summoning of the "Mother of a Thousand Wings"—an ancient demon of pestilence
  • Willowshore revealed to sit at a convergence of ley lines—arcane geomancy paths that mirror the five rivers on the surface
  • Mido disclosed secret entrances into the Yeshou estate (now occupied by the magistrate)
  • Yong delivered runed weapons to the party; confirmed plans to leave for a coastal town after the festival
  • Hong reported no further sabotage plots among the town's children
  • The Festival of Returning Spirits is set for the next evening

docs.title: Session Four (2026-02-26)
docs.text:
• The Festival of Returning Spirits took place: procession, tea transfer ceremony at the Seven Colored Songbird Theater, ceremonial dance, and feast
  • Mayor Masru arrived with four red-skinned oni guards—surprisingly unimposing, affable, and food-obsessed
  • Mido formally transferred power to Masru via the tea ceremony
  • A moth swarm destroyed five lanterns at the theater, alarming both Magistrate Kurosawa and Mido
  • Meilin the gravekeeper stunned the town with her transformation during the dance
  • A dwarven skeleton (Kaizo clan) was discovered in an old dry well
  • Liwen the florist revealed Kurosawa ordered five dozen white lilies (funeral flowers)
  • The party infiltrated the Yeshou estate via three routes: firefly through a window, koi pond tunnel, and shed tunnel
  • A fox construct alarm triggered in the magistrate's bedroom; Kurosawa rushed back to the estate
  • The Yeshou estate's koi pond passage is guarded by a mutated koi fish

docs.title: Session Five (2026-03-12)
docs.text:
• The party escaped the estate: Donkey as a firefly, Da Baishan through the front door with a bluff, Littlefinger through the shadows after stealing a military medal
  • Martial law declared by Mayor Masru and Magistrate Kurosawa—all citizens confined to homes, gatherings criminal, travel forbidden; decrees nailed across both sides of town
  • Oni guards actively patrolled both banks, escorting citizens home and confronting those outside
  • Donkey used Conceal Spell to cast Sleep on an oni guard enforcing the lockdown
  • The party was escorted back to Silver Mist Inn under guard
  • Mido revealed the existence of Gosembiki (五芒星, the Five Pointed Star)—haunted ruins 10–20 miles east of Willowshore, connected to the ley line convergence
  • Luda, a local seamstress and arcane supplier, reported suspicious ingredient purchases by Kurosawa
  • The town is now under active lockdown; the magistrate plans to investigate the estate break-in

docs.title: Session Six (2026-03-19)
docs.text:
• A shared dream spread through the town—multiple residents including the party, Mayor Masru, and Radiant Willow experienced vivid visions of the land crying out in pain, rivers running black, and ley lines warping under pressure
  • Kurosawa ransacked the party's rooms at Silver Mist Inn as part of his investigation
  • Mayor Masru hired the party as "Masru's Faithful Five" with daily stipends and investigative licenses, overriding Kurosawa's authority
  • The Yeshou family was sentenced to exile in five days by Kurosawa
  • Meilin now appears to serve as a personal attendant to the mayor at the estate
  • Captain Akoto identified as one of the oni guard captains patrolling the town
  • The party tested their credentials, questioned Akoto, visited the Yeshous, Radiant Willow, and the cemetery before leaving town east toward the Gosembiki ruins
  • One of Mido's guards was found transformed into an infected werewolf 8+ miles east of town and killed by the party

docs.title: Session Eight (2026-04-22)
docs.text:
• A chasm tore through town from the east, splitting farmland and buildings along a line parallel to the river—an aftershock of the party pulling Kurosawa's device from the Gosembiki ruins
  • Demons began climbing out of the chasm—three emerged on the first night; one was killed by the party, one by Kurosawa in a single nodachi swing, and one dove back into the rift
  • At least one commoner was killed in the street; livestock and river-fish were killed by the chasm's heat
  • Kurosawa invoked the Rite of Open Reckoning—an ancient Chu Ye legal procedure—against the party; Mayor Masru served as judge
  • Verdict: guilty of unlawful interference, reckless endangerment, and spiritual disruption. The party was disarmed and marched to a warehouse.
  • Radiant Willow was the only townsperson to raise her hand when Boone asked the crowd who had shared the dream
  • The Seven Colored Songbird Theater and the square around it served as the trial site

docs.title: Session Nine (2026-05-07)
docs.text:
• The party fled west along the riverside out of town immediately at session start; Kurosawa and two oni gave chase across the grasslands beyond the town edge
  • Kurosawa demonstrated open geomantic combat in the chase: an earthen-grasp that pinned Boone, a 5 ft × 10 ft earthen wall raised across the party's escape line. Kurosawa critically struck Boone twice, dropping him to 0 HP, and sliced Littlefinger near to death
  • Radiant Willow ran out of town toward the fight unarmed and pleading. Kurosawa hesitated, lowered his nodachi, and dropped the wall. The party surrendered out of respect for her
  • Marched back into town and held in a fishy warehouse near the river (~40 ft × 50 ft, no windows, double doors barred) under one oni guard at a time, four oni in shifts
  • The Yeshou family extracted the party at night through a floor-hatch into a smuggling tunnel under the warehouse — part of a much older network beneath Willowshore that the party had no idea existed
  • The hidden papers (including a damning planning note in Kurosawa's hand) were retrieved from the wall crevice north of town by Littlefinger, still where he hid them
  • Townspeople — Yong among them, who "shook his head, disappointed" — stood at street-edges and watched the party marched in, and stayed silent
  • After the escape the party crossed the river south of town and left Willowshore, headed for the Order of the Palatine Eye. The Yeshous remain inside, watching from hideouts

docs.title: Session Eleven (2026-06-04)
docs.text:
• The town did not appear directly, but the party learned the shape of the threat against it. The pool at the Hollow of Seven Cedars showed Kurosawa's Root rite already corrupting Willowshore's memory — neighbors forgetting kindnesses, Liwen not recognizing the party, Radiant Willow forgetting why she trusted them, Yong re-remembering the party as the cause of his son's danger. The corruption flows from the cedars into the town
  • The party's fight to save Willowshore is now explicitly a fight for the town's memory of itself, not just its safety — and the only known cure (killing the grove) carries its own heavy cost

docs.title: Session Twelve (2026-07-16)
docs.text:
• The Grandmother confirmed the corruption is real and already done: the town's good memories of the party are eaten and cannot be restored — "what went downhill must remain downhill." Reversing the rite will only stop further damage
  • The party returned and surveilled the town from the northwest tree line: life looked outwardly normal (the eastern chasm scar still visible), but the oni garrison has doubled to ~8 red-skinned guards, Kurosawa was nowhere to be seen, and a new blue-skinned oni administrator now issues orders from the Yeshou estate — obeyed even by Captain Akoto
  • Under cover of night, the party executed a clean heist of the estate — Donkey as a dragonfly through Kurosawa's office window, Littlefinger picking the lacquered chest's lock — stealing the Root Correction ritual, five copper nails, and Kurosawa's lockbox note. The fox construct arrived moments too late; no alarm was raised
  • The party withdrew west into the forest the same night; as far as they know, the town is unaware they were ever there

docs.title: Session Fourteen (2026-08-20)
docs.text:
• The curse's spread is over — the party completed the reversal at the Hollow of Seven Cedars, freeing the Grandmother and permanently stopping the corruption flowing down the ley line into town. The damage already done remains
  • The party walked back in and saw what the curse has made of the town (Donkey, Society 21): outwardly normal, inwardly cold — no banter, no clusters of conversation, people transactional and standoffish, "siloish." The community that made Willowshore itself is missing
  • Hong and Yong are in open feud — a shouting, public rift; Hong left the forge with a packed bag, heading south, his father calling good riddance behind him. Nobody in town intervened
  • The curse's pattern confirmed (GM): those most affected are the people who interacted most with the party or Kurosawa — Hong and Yong worst of all; Radiant Willow heavily tainted but bent toward self-doubt by her optimism
  • The first cure: Willow ate half the Grandmother's seed at Dew Drop Petals and was restored completely — the party's one public ally is back, "You've saved our town. Or at least me"
  • Kurosawa returned from Cloudbreaker Cairn, audibly displeased — and walked alone into Dew Drop Petals to demand the party "quietly, civilly surrender" for violating their exile. The party is leaning toward answering with their own Rite of Open Reckoning
  • Post-session GM retcon: the town has a spirit of its own that could consume the seed and cleanse everyone — see The Spirit of Willowshore above

docs.title: Session Fifteen (2026-09-03)
docs.text:
• A new power arrived: Magistrate Atsura of the Mirror Tribunal — the Council of the Magi's internal affairs — is in town (two days as of this session) to investigate Kurosawa, operating from the Yeshou estate
  • The party surrendered civilly and was held in a purpose-built cage in the estate courtyard — then freed the same day by Atsura's ruling: their sentence confines them to Willowshore's borders, not to a cell. They walk the town openly, watched but lawful
  • The town's post-curse temperament held: leery, transactional, paranoid — people sitting alone, short sentences, occasional flare-ups of argument. Not hostile, just hollow. Radiant Willow remains the one bright spot, skipping across the street to greet the freed party
  • The town spirit was named: Old Amber, the golden-koi river spirit, silent ~two years — since before the oni. Mido (back in her suite at the Silver Mist Inn, its concierge desk now unmanned) supplied the lore; the route to the spirit runs through the Land of Dreams
  • Luda's flower shop supplied nightshade and poppy for the deep-sleep brew (9 gp, minus the 6 Littlefinger stole back); the brew was crafted and drunk in the back rooms of Dew Drop Petals, with Donkey and Littlefinger crossing into the dream of Willowshore — a warped, mirrored painting of the town — where the Mother of a Thousand Wings waits tethered to five lanterns

docs.title: Session Sixteen (2026-09-17)
docs.text:
• The memory curse is lifted from the entire town. Old Amber, freed from its dream-prison by the party, consumed the Grandmother's seed — see The Curse Lifted above. The river quickened, fish leapt into nets, the reeds bloomed, and Yong and Hong embraced in the square
  • The town turned. Townsfolk thanked the party in the street; Yong apologized for his silence at the trial; a dock worker at the Silver Mist Inn — full and loud for the first time in memory — poured them half his cider and called the day "a turning point for Willowshore"
  • Public confrontation in the square: Willow credited the "so-called fugitives" with saving the town; Kurosawa called the party "an evil, dark part of Willowshore" and demanded their re-arrest; Atsura refused — "they are abiding by the ruling." Kurosawa retreated to the estate fuming
  • Masru apologized and handed over Kurosawa's handwritten script for the first Reckoning's verdict; Atsura declared her investigation "nearly complete" and offered the party a choice between her verdict and their own Second Reckoning
  • A festival was called for sundown to celebrate Old Amber's return and the sudden bounty of fish; the town spent the afternoon hanging decorations and preparing food
  • Meilin remains confined to the Yeshou estate with Masru — bruised, frightened, and denying it — while the mayor lobbies to take her back to Kirahata
  • The second curse entered the record via Old Amber's warning; the party took the question straight to the Yeshou suite at the Silver Mist Inn, where Cheng said "Treats" and Mido looked nervous

docs.title: Magistrate Atsura
docs.text: "I am not your enemy. I am not Kurosawa's enemy. I'm here to understand what is going on and what is the truth."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Atsura (initially reported by Mido's network as "Otsuru") Ancestry Tiefling oni (blue-skinned) Role Magistrate of the Council of the Magi; agent of the Mirror Tribunal Affiliation The Council of the Magi — sent to investigate Kurosawa, not to assist him Location Willowshore, operating out of the occupied Yeshou estate Status Active ally-in-practice; freed the party from their cage (Session Fifteen); investigation of Kurosawa "nearly complete" — verdict pending the party's choice (Session Sixteen)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A small blue-skinned tiefling oni woman, perhaps 5'6" — nothing like Kurosawa's seven-foot menace or the Mayor's girth. She wears no war gear: a samurai-style breastplate over light, robe-like clothes that drape through her forearms, maybe a dagger at most. The party's first read from the tree line was "maybe a wizard, maybe an accountant" — and both turned out to be closer than they knew.

Her most distinctive feature: dense tattoos running up from her wrists in full arm sleeves — and several of them are arcane tattoos, unique among every oni the party has seen. Da Baishan's read (Perception 19): none are offensive. They are abjuration, warding, and scrying work — protective and investigative magic, worn on the skin. One of them visibly shimmered with tracing light when she authenticated the party's documentary evidence.

What she lacks in stature she holds in rank. Guards hand her their keys when she says "keys." Kurosawa starts shouting when she frees his prisoners — and composes himself the moment she raises a hand.

docs.title: Role: The Mirror Tribunal
docs.text:
Atsura carries the full authority of the Council of the Magi and the Mirror Tribunal — the Council's internal-affairs arm, which polices magistrates "who may be using their station or the learned elements from it in a way that is not in accordance to our credo."

  • She was dispatched because of "disturbing echoes and reverberations" — the ripples and spikes of ley-line energy — emanating from the Willowshore area
  • Her assignment is explicitly to find the truth of what Kurosawa is up to; there was already evidence against him before she arrived
  • She has been in Willowshore only two days (as of Session Fifteen) and arrived unannounced — Kurosawa was visibly, briefly shocked to find her waiting outside Dew Drop Petals
  • Her method is evidence-first: "It can't be based on my eyes. Maybe based on your eyes. I need something that is proof."

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Courteous, dry, and unhurried — she answers Kurosawa's rapid-fire questions with "I'll tell you when I've learned enough." She respects the law even when she plainly dislikes its results: she confirmed the party's Rite of Open Reckoning conviction was "a legal proceeding up to all the codes and conducts therein of that ancient right" (crediting Kurosawa's encyclopedic knowledge of dead statutes with a lawyer's mix of admiration and distaste), then found the seam in it — the sentence confines the party to Willowshore, not to a cage.

She smiles more than any oni official the party has met. She winked at Boone. The party is still deciding what that means; Boone is not.

"Unfortunately, no boyfriend. Travels are long, hours are long, and it's a demanding road."

docs.title: What She Knows / Has Verified
docs.text:
• The party's evidence is authentic. Her tattoo-magic examined Kurosawa's signed device-commission note and one of the seven cursed copper nails: "There seems to be no arcane or illusionary script... I believe it's authentic. What you said and what this evidence shows seems to align directly"
  • Kurosawa has been planning something for a while — her words — and she believes the energy spike from the area is his influence
  • The party told her about the memory curse on the town (so she knows testimony from townsfolk is compromised) and their plan to lift it
  • She has not been told about the plum, the Grandmother, or the Land of Dreams expedition — only that the party needs "a few hours without Kurosawa snooping around," which she agreed to provide
  • She has seen Masru's trial script — Kurosawa's handwritten instructions for the first Reckoning's verdict — and heard the mayor's public apology (Session Sixteen). Her assessment: the original trial was "a sham, a kangaroo court" that she "cannot defend in any of my verdict"

docs.title: The Offer (Session Sixteen)
docs.text:
With the memory curse lifted and the mayor's script in hand, Atsura told the party her investigation was nearly complete — "I have found all the evidence I believe I need to cast my verdict" — and drew the jurisdictional line carefully: "I am not part of the municipality that can free your name. My investigation is on Kurosawa himself and his stance with the Order and Council of the Magi."

Then she gave them a choice:

  1. She casts her verdict on Kurosawa now. "I don't know exactly what that outcome would be" — though she believes the party has "a good intuition" of it
  2. The party holds its Second Rite of Open Reckoning first, and she casts her verdict afterward

"The reason I'm giving you this opportunity is I'm not exactly sure you will have an opportunity afterward once my verdict is cast."

The party asked for time to consult. She agreed and walked off with Masru lobbying at her elbow. Beforehand she made a muttered aside about "5,000 gold pieces" that went unexplained — the price of Masru's commission, a bounty, a fine, or something else entirely.

The party is split on her. Boone: "I think she's great." Donkey: "She hands us our freedom on a silver platter, and there's this other curse Kurosawa was investigating... she's up to something. We need to know more about this old curse before we do any deals with her."

docs.title: Boone
docs.text: Whatever "psychic connection" Boone attempted through the doorway (Performance — she smirked and shook her head), the private garden conversation worked: she called his eyes honest, took his evidence seriously, and freed the party on his word plus paper. His parting smolder earned a smile and a wink. Boone walked away "on clouds." Willow has already offered him the full head-to-toe treatment: "You will look irresistible."

docs.title: Kurosawa
docs.text: Colleagues in title, adversaries in fact. He did not know she was in town; his beat of visible surprise at the door — caught by Boone — was the first crack in his composure the party has ever seen. She outranks him in practice: she countermanded his caging of the party to his face, and he swallowed it.

docs.title: The Party
docs.text: "I am not your enemy." She is using them as an evidence source against Kurosawa, and they are using her as legal cover — both sides know it, and so far the arrangement is holding. She freed them from the cage on her own ruling: "They are confined to the borders of Willowshore. That is what they were convicted of. And they will honor that."

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• What verdict is she building toward — and what does a Mirror Tribunal sentence against a magistrate of Kurosawa's stature look like?
  • How much of the truth can the party afford to give her? The plum, the spirit realm, and their own rule-bending (the estate heist, the stolen ritual pages) are all still off the books
  • The name discrepancy — Mido's network reported her as Otsuru; she introduces herself as Atsura. Bad intel, or two names?
  • Is Boone right? (Increasingly, embarrassingly: yes)

docs.title: Session Twelve (2026-07-16)
docs.text:
• First observed from the tree line northwest of Willowshore during the party's pre-heist surveillance
  • Noted commanding guards (including Captain Akoto) from the Yeshou estate, unarmed, in Kurosawa's absence
  • Not encountered directly; the party's estate heist that night avoided all contact

docs.title: Session Thirteen (2026-08-13)
docs.text:
• Named by Mido's intelligence network (as "Otsuru"): a young tiefling oni magistrate of the Council of the Magi, who arrived leading a new group
  • The party matched her to the administrator they had watched from the trees: "Yeah, we noticed her"
  • Reported to be studying in the estate, questioning Masru, and commanding the town's other oni leaders — all of whom defer to her despite her youth

docs.title: Session Fifteen (2026-09-03)
docs.text:
• Formally introduced herself — as Magistrate Atsura — waiting with the guard detail outside Dew Drop Petals when Kurosawa marched the party out to their new cage. His flash of surprise on seeing her (caught by Boone, Perception 22) confirmed she was not part of his plan
  • Identified by Boone's lore (19) as an agent of the Mirror Tribunal — the Council of the Magi's internal affairs — meaning Kurosawa knows exactly why she's here
  • Came back to the courtyard cage alone within the hour to interview the party: "I'm giving you an opportunity to tell me what is your truth" — while confirming she'd verify everything against Willow's testimony, the townsfolk, and her own arcane instruments
  • Took Boone to a private garden table, where he presented Kurosawa's signed device-commission note and a cursed copper nail; her arcane tattoo traced the parchment and pronounced it authentic. Her verdict: "You have honest eyes. I believe you're telling the truth here"
  • Freed the party from the cage on her own legal reading: the Open Reckoning sentence confines them to Willowshore's borders, not to a cell — "Whether you're in a cage or not... we are obeying the intent of that law." Demanded the guard's keys twice; got them twice
  • Faced down Kurosawa publicly when he emerged shouting at the sight of the party walking free — one raised hand, a quiet exchange, and he went back inside
  • Agreed to keep Kurosawa occupied for several hours while the party worked on lifting the curse: "He and I have a few things to discuss anyway"
  • Answered Boone's "Is your boyfriend also a magistrate?" with a chuckle and a workaholic's lament; answered his parting smolder (Performance 13) with a smile and a wink

docs.title: Session Sixteen (2026-09-17)
docs.text:
• Walked out of the estate three abreast with Masru and Kurosawa as the lifted curse rippled through town; was hugged by Willow — surprised, didn't push her off, smirked
  • Shut Kurosawa down publicly a second time. When he demanded of Masru why convicted "fugitives" were free to roam, she answered for the mayor: "They haven't broken any of the rulings cast down on them from the Rite of Open Reckoning. They haven't left the city limits and they will not. They are abiding by the ruling"
  • Witnessed Masru's confession and the handover of Kurosawa's verdict script to Da Baishan; the mayor visibly played to her while surrendering it
  • Declared her investigation "nearly complete" and laid out the offer: her verdict now, or the party's Second Reckoning first — warning that the window may close once she rules. Granted the party time to consult: "Very well"
  • Left with Masru pleading for his commission to be voided so he can return to Kirahata with Meilin; her answer, if any, was not heard

docs.title: Captain Akoto
docs.text: A soldier doing his job in a town that doesn't want him.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Akoto Title Captain Ancestry Oni (red-skinned) Affiliation Magistrate Kurosawa's guard detachment Location Willowshore

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Captain Akoto is one of the red-skinned oni guards serving under Magistrate Kurosawa. He patrols the streets of Willowshore enforcing martial law. Unlike the magistrate, Akoto appears to be a straightforward soldier—he follows orders without relish and seems somewhat reasonable when presented with legitimate authority.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Akoto is professional and measured. When the party presented their investigative licenses from Mayor Masru, he was confused but compliant. He did not enjoy the confrontation and moved on without incident. He was willing to share basic information when asked directly, admitting that the troops were told very little about the investigation.

docs.title: Session Six (2026-03-19)
docs.text:
• Confronted the party on the street during martial law; ordered them back to their homes
  • Read the party's investigative licenses from Mayor Masru; looked confused but let them pass
  • When Ginkgo demanded his name and rank, he paused but complied: "Captain Akoto"
  • Admitted the troops were told very little by Kurosawa—only to enforce the lockdown and ensure no one leaves town
  • Confirmed Kurosawa was first on the scene at the estate and insisted on handling the investigation alone
  • Said he guessed the lockdown related to the commotion at the estate; expressed mild doubt: "I don't think Kurosawa will be as calm as I am"

docs.title: Session Eight (2026-04-22)
docs.text:
• Present during the demon attack on Willowshore; engaged one of the creatures alongside his fellow oni guards and townsfolk before the party arrived
  • Called as a prosecution witness during the Rite of Open Reckoning
  • Testified that he encountered the party leaving town toward the eastern ruins, and that they had stopped at the graveyard first "conversing in secret—possibly with the dead"
  • Did not mention that Donkey had put him to Sleep with Conceal Spell during martial law (either from omission, tact, or not knowing)
  • Concluded that the party "acted on their own authority, sought no counsel, and reported to no one"
  • Professional and measured in tone; offered no personal animosity, but delivered testimony that supported Kurosawa's framing of the party as unsanctioned operators

docs.title: Session Twelve (2026-07-16)
docs.text: • Observed from a distance during the party's surveillance of Willowshore: still on duty amid a garrison doubled to ~8 guards, and now following the orders of the new blue-skinned oni administrator operating from the estate in Kurosawa's absence

docs.title: Cassian Voss
docs.text: A scholar of forgotten gods, now a forgotten ghost.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Cassian Voss Ancestry Human (presumed) Occupation Religious researcher / Scholar of "old gods" Origin Absalom (foreign continent) Status Deceased — spirit untethered Location Willowshore (spirit)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Cassian Voss was a religious researcher from Absalom—a continent far from Tian Xia, making him one of the very few foreigners ever to pass through Willowshore. He arrived roughly two months before Magistrate Kurosawa, stayed for about a week, and then supposedly moved on to continue his research elsewhere.

In death, he appears as a translucent blue-white spirit—shimmering like heat haze off summer stone. Water drips from his face and the tattered sleeves of clothing that is distinctly not from Willowshore. He does not remember his own name.

docs.title: Research
docs.text:
Voss specialized in what he called "old gods"—elder deities that predated the current known pantheon across all traditions. His theory held that before the gods worshipped today, there existed a group of ancient, primordial entities—similar to how Greek mythology's Titans preceded the Olympians.

He came to Tian Xia specifically because its pantheon was unfamiliar to Absalom's scholars, and he hoped to find histories, oral traditions, or other links to these elder gods among the local religious practices. Very little is known about these entities, and Voss's work represented a rare scholarly effort to catalog them.

His research interests align disturbingly well with the dark summoning ritual later discovered at the Mourndusk Willow—a ritual that Mido identified as an invocation of the "Mother of a Thousand Wings", an ancient demon of pestilence.

Session Ten established that Voss carried the eye-mark of the Order of the Palatine Eye on the back of his hand — the same mark the cliff drew on Da Baishan. Session Eleven added the rest of the picture: Voss was at the Hollow of Seven Cedars, investigating the leyline that runs through it, six months to a year ago — months before Kurosawa drove his nails. He was, in other words, an Order investigator who found the grove before it was corrupted, and did not survive the finding.

docs.title: Death and Spirit
docs.text:
Voss was killed by a spirit at the river near Willowshore. Only Da Baishan and Ginkgo witnessed the death. Following Ginkgo's beliefs about the natural cycle, they hid the body in the forest rather than following local customs for spirit-death disposal.

Since then, Voss's spirit has appeared to Da Baishan and Ginkgo on multiple occasions:

  • During the graveyard combat (Session Two), the spirit appeared and shielded Da Baishan from the undead cat's attack
  • He spoke cryptic words: "You carry me into earth that is not my own. My ties bind beyond these roots. Something stolen, something broken."
  • He cannot cross to the afterlife until the mystery of his death is solved

docs.title: Personality (In Life)
docs.text: Based on Donkey's memories, Voss was a quiet, studious man who kept mostly to himself during his brief stay. He was noticeable primarily because foreigners from Absalom are exceedingly rare in this part of the world. He showed no signs of hostility or ill intent—just scholarly curiosity—and his departure seemed unremarkable at the time.

docs.title: The Carving at the Grove (Session Eleven)
docs.text:
On the third cedar of the Hollow of Seven Cedars, about 20 inches off the ground, Boone's "That's Odd" turned up a name that had been carved and then frantically scratched out with a blade — leaving only ·S·S·I·N·V·O·S·S. Da Baishan's recall pieced it into Cassian Voss. Around the gouges was a fine, mustard-khaki powder that Da Baishan identified (Occultism) as finely-ground moth-wing carapace — the same signature as the inauguration moths and the Mourndusk Willow wings.

Da Baishan's quick magic-identification placed the carving and powder at six months to a year old — faintly magical, older than Kurosawa's recent nail-and-graft work (which dates within a month of the party's arrival in Willowshore). Cross-referenced against the party's belief that Voss died ~6 months ago, the timeline lines up: Voss was at the grove, investigating its leyline, before Kurosawa got there, and his name was defaced around the time he died. The handwriting also looked familiar to Littlefinger — not Kurosawa's, but something he'd seen before and couldn't place.

This reframes Voss from a Willowshore curiosity into a predecessor: an Order investigator working the exact site that has now become Kurosawa's Root key, who got close enough to be killed and scrubbed from the tree.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• How did he actually die? — He was killed by a spirit at the river; the grove sits on that leyline. Was the grove (or its Warden, or the Dream Eater) what killed him — or did whatever Kurosawa later weaponized already stir there?
  • Who scratched out his name on the third cedar, and why? Kurosawa, to erase a predecessor? The grove itself? Voss, defacing his own mark?
  • Whose handwriting did Littlefinger half-recognize in the carving?
  • Is his death connected to the ritual? — He was Order, he was on the leyline, and he predates Kurosawa at the very site that is now the rite's keystone
  • What was "stolen" and "broken"? — His spirit's cryptic message suggests something was taken from him and something was violated or destroyed
  • Did someone else benefit from his death? — Could the ritual have required a sacrifice, and was Voss that sacrifice?

docs.title: Session Zero (2026-01-16)
docs.text:
• Da Baishan and Ginkgo witnessed his death by spirit at the river
  • His body was hidden in the forest against local custom

docs.title: Session Two (2026-02-05)
docs.text:
• His spirit appeared during the graveyard combat; shielded Da Baishan from the undead cat
  • Delivered cryptic message: "Something stolen, something broken"
  • Could not remember his own name or identity

docs.title: Session Three (2026-02-12)
docs.text:
• Identified by Donkey (Willowshore Lore 26) as Cassian Voss, a religious researcher from Absalom
  • His specialty in "old gods" / elder deities established
  • His timeline in Willowshore (arriving ~2 months before the magistrate) raises questions about the ritual's timeline

docs.title: Session Four (2026-02-26)
docs.text:
• Radiant Willow shared additional details from her conversations with Voss:
    • He described "five lines, five fortunes" converging at Willowshore—aligning with the ley line convergence Mido revealed
    • He said "something is being drawn here"—the only thing about his research that seemed to worry him
    • His last known plans were to head east, following the rivers where the ley lines tracked
    • He had originally wanted to go north into the Dark Woods, but Willow warned him against it
    • Willow described him as "an amazing researcher" who was "so excited" about his findings—she still believes he simply moved on

docs.title: Session Six (2026-03-19)
docs.text:
• His spirit was channeled through Da Baishan during a cemetery séance led by the party (Spirit Lore 18, Diplomacy check); spoke through Da Baishan's body while Da Baishan could hear but not control himself
  • The spirit was taxing and could answer only a few questions before fading:
    • On the old gods: "There were five. Despite the current understanding, they are much closer than the legends would like us to believe. It is not very difficult to commune with them." Also: "They are clever manipulators and to be seriously concerned."
    • On who benefits from bringing them back: "Foolish ones seeking power."
    • On the prophecy (artist, ruler, sage, lover, judge): "That is the ritual for the Unspeakable One. Five must be sacrificed to bring—" (cut off mid-sentence; the spirit was pulled away)
  • The Unspeakable One — a new entity identified by Voss's spirit as the target of a sacrifice ritual involving the five archetypes from the prophecy
  • His knowledge of the old gods continues to prove critical to the party's investigation even in death

docs.title: Session Ten (2026-05-14)
docs.text: • Recalled by Da Baishan at the Palatine Eye Vault: Voss carried the same eye-mark on the back of his hand that the cliff door drew — first hard evidence he was Order, or Order-marked

docs.title: Session Eleven (2026-06-04)
docs.text:
• His name was found carved and scratched out on the third cedar of the Hollow of Seven Cedars, packed with ground moth-wing powder — see The Carving at the Grove above
  • The carving dated 6 months to a year old, months before Kurosawa's corruption of the grove — establishing Voss as an Order investigator who reached the site first and died there
  • Littlefinger found the handwriting familiar but could not place it — explicitly not Kurosawa's

docs.title: Session Twelve (2026-07-16)
docs.text:
• The erasure of his name was confirmed to be a second, separate seal on the grove — see the two seals. Kurosawa's stolen lockbox note admits: "The name was taken before I came to the cedars. The powder is not mine." Even the magistrate does not know whose hand it was
  • The party's camp analysis characterized the erasure as done in "haste, emotion, emotional removal" — nothing like geomancy — in a script Donkey half-recognizes and cannot place
  • Ginkgo floated Voss himself as the second seal's author ("Who else would it be? Could it be Cassian Voss?"); Da Baishan: "He's all over this... I knew we should have buried him"
  • The Grandmother's reversal instructions — "give back the name and undo the seals" — may point directly at his scratched-out name

docs.title: Session Fourteen (2026-08-20)
docs.text:
• His name was given back. Da Baishan carved Cassian Voss into the third cedar in his best handwriting, directly above the frantic erasure — step four of the reversal at the Hollow of Seven Cedars
  • The erasure fought back: at the second S, the moth-wing powder spun off the tree into a screaming creature of sand and dust — the second seal's residue given form, intent solely on stopping the carving. The party destroyed it, and Da Baishan finished the letters

  • With the name restored, his voice reached Da Baishan one more time — raspy, fainter and weaker than before, but unmistakable:

    "Tell the Order — it was not the oni."

  • The message lands as his clearest testimony yet on his own death and on the second hand at the cedars: whoever erased his name — and likely whoever killed him — was not Kurosawa and not the oni. The GM's closing recap tied it together: a second ritual, linked to Voss and the Order of the Palatine Eye, predates everything Kurosawa built at the grove

  • Whether returning his name (and freeing the Grandmother) is enough to finally untether his spirit remains to be seen — his voice was weaker than before, not stronger

docs.title: Cliché
docs.text: "What could be more cliché than a blind man giving wise advice in the mountains?"

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name "Cliché" (self-given) Title / Role Mountain hermit; oracle on the road to the Order of the Palatine Eye Ancestry Halfling (apparent) — "about the size of a toddler, three and a half feet" Location A switchback landing in the mountains south of Willowshore, roughly halfway between Glutton's Bridge and the Palatine Eye Vault Status Walked off camp without anyone seeing him leave

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A small, scrawny figure hunched beside a stone-ringed coal fire on a narrow mountain landing. Tattered Tibet-style fur wraps for warmth. An old straw hat. Cloth wraps wound entirely over the eyes. No one in the party has ever seen what is, or is not, behind them.

He poked the coals with a walking stick when the party crested the switchback. Round, dark, almost-perfect spheres of stone — he kept them in the fire and would, on some private signal, reach down for one and use it as a gift, or a punctuation mark.

When the party left, his stones were still in the fire pit. The fire was still warm. The hermit was gone, and there were no tracks.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Cliché speaks in compressed, oblique riddle-talk — only ever as much as the listener can carry, never the literal answer. He never names anything by its proper name within earshot. The Order is "the eye." Kurosawa is "the smiling one" and Cheng Yesho is referenced obliquely. The PCs are not given their own names back; instead they are labeled by what he sees in them:

PC Cliché's name for them Boone Truth Hound — "You've come in search of the eye." Da Baishan "One small scan." Donkey The One Who Makes Sparks Ginkgo (greeted with a smile; offered the stone) Littlefinger (greeted; not labeled aloud)

He is unhurried, friendly in a clipped way, and faintly amused — a man who has waited for travelers like this before, and will wait again.

docs.title: What He Knows He Should Not
docs.text:
A society check (Donkey, 26) found that the hermit knows things a mountain recluse should not:

  • He named the smiling one — meaning Cheng Yesho — without ever being given the name
  • He clearly knew about Magistrate Kurosawa
  • He knew Da Baishan was on the road to the eye — without saying Order or Palatine aloud
  • Asked about Vujravati, he answered without hesitation: "the celestial one — through cycles of time, has seen the rise and fall of civilizations and the gods themselves. A great asset is the celestial one."

He does not appear in any Willowshore story Donkey or Da Baishan can recall, nor in any traveler's description of the southern mountains. Society 26 produced no recognition at all.

docs.title: The Three Roads
docs.text:
Asked which path the party should take, Cliché gave them, in order:

"Go south, find the eye. Go west, cut the root. Go back, save the town. All roads are dire. The question is not which road is safe. There is no safe road. The question is — which wound can you bear?"

This is the first explicit framing of the campaign's three open fronts as a single triage problem rather than a sequence.

docs.title: Notable Quotes
docs.text:
"Late, you are early. Always rushing, truth seekers. Never asking if the truth wishes to be found, though. Come, come — sit."

"You walk thinking truth awaits, like a lantern. But truth is not a lantern. Truth is a knife. It cuts rope, yes — and also the hand of those who uncovered too much."

"A thing buried is not always buried by cowards. Sometimes buried by the wise."

"Seek the cliff that has no door. Knock with the hand that doubts. And when truth speaks kindly, distrust it most."

"Knowledge found. Keep nose to ground, mind to thread. That's good. Good — but careful. Some tracks follow you back."

docs.title: Gifts
docs.text:
• A warm hand-stone to each of the four PCs who would take one — small, dark, perfectly round stones from the coals of his fire. They hold heat for hours; ideal for a pocket or a sleeve in mountain cold. No visible markings; no obvious magic. "It'll warm your hands."

He gave one to Da Baishan as he stood and tossed the rest. Then the party looked back, and he was gone.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Who or what is Cliché actually? A halfling oracle? Something pretending to be a halfling? An agent of the Order? An agent of something the Order was founded to watch?
  • Do the stones do more than warm hands? They were sitting in his fire as if waiting for someone.
  • He knew Cheng Yesho's epithet without being told. He knew Vujravati. What else does he know that he didn't volunteer?
  • "Some tracks follow you back." What did the party draw with them on the road south?

docs.title: Session Ten (2026-05-14)
docs.text:
• Encountered on a switchback landing about halfway up the mountain south of Glutton's Bridge, an hour or so after the ham-trebuchet detour
  • Greeted the party by their internal natures rather than their names — "truth hound," "the one who makes sparks"
  • Refused to confirm his real name; chose the placeholder "Cliché"
  • Confirmed Vujravati by epithet — "the celestial one"
  • Confirmed the campaign's three quest lines as "all roads are dire" — south, west, and back to Willowshore
  • Spoke the riddle that solved the door of the Palatine Eye Vault: "Seek the cliff that has no door. Knock with the hand that doubts."
  • Gifted each PC who would take one a warm hand-stone from his fire
  • Vanished without footprints while the party was still standing on the landing

docs.title: Session Eleven (2026-06-04)
docs.text: • Did not appear, but his warm hand-stones earned their keep: the party used them to heat food at a cold, fireless camp on the road northwest to the Hollow of Seven Cedars, avoiding a campfire that would have given away their position. The stones still hold heat hours later, as advertised — and the open question of whether they do more than warm hands remains open

docs.title: Hong
docs.text: A boy with firework dreams and a bag full of someone else's gold.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Hong Age ~10 years old Ancestry Kitsune Occupation Blacksmith's son / apprentice Location Eternal Blaze Ironworks, Willowshore

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Hong is Yong's young son—a kitsune boy of about ten years old, energetic and impulsive. He has a restless spirit and dreams of leaving Willowshore for open skies and wide seas, far from the dense forests and small-town life he's known.

Despite his youth, Hong is perceptive enough to recognize opportunity and desperate enough to take dangerous risks for his family's sake.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Hong is earnest, loyal to his father, and terrible at lying. When confronted by the party at Silver Mist Lodge, his attempts at deception were transparent—darting eyes, stammered excuses, and a visible urge to flee. Once he felt safe enough to talk, his words tumbled out with the unfiltered honesty of a child who knows he's in over his head.

He is not malicious. The warehouse fire was meant to be a "prank"—he genuinely did not intend for anyone to get hurt. He invited Kimmy along to "see the fireworks," not realizing the danger.

docs.title: The Warehouse Job
docs.text:
Hong was hired by the Yeshou family to destroy the fireworks stored for the Festival of Returning Spirits. The details:

  • Payment: 100 gold pieces
  • Instructions: Cause a "prank" that would disrupt the festival by destroying the fireworks
  • Method: Hong used kerosene to ensure all the boxes of fireworks would ignite at once, since lighting them individually seemed impractical
  • The girl: Kimmy was not part of the plan; Hong invited her along
  • The fire: Got out of control far beyond what Hong expected; the party rescued both children

Hong met with the Yeshou family alone. He does not know if they hired anyone else for similar jobs.

docs.title: Yong (Father)
docs.text: Hong idolizes his father and took the dangerous job specifically to help him. Yong has been talking about leaving Willowshore—he "sees dark skies ahead"—but lacks the funds to relocate and re-establish his forge elsewhere. The 100 gold would make that possible.

docs.title: The Party
docs.text: Hong is grateful to the party for rescuing him from the fire and for securing his payment from the Yeshou family. He trusts them, particularly Boone, with whom he had an extended conversation about life beyond Willowshore—open seas, wide skies, places far from forests.

docs.title: Boone
docs.text: While the rest of the party met with Mido, Hong stayed behind with Boone at Silver Mist Lodge. He was fascinated by the dwarf's stories of distant lands and showed little interest in mountains or forests, preferring tales of open coastlines and wide horizons.

docs.title: Session One (2026-01-30)
docs.text:
• Trapped in the burning warehouse along with Kimmy
  • Rescued by Littlefinger and Ginkgo
  • Whispered "It wasn't my fault" after being pulled free
  • Burns treated with Da Baishan's salve

docs.title: Session Two (2026-02-05)
docs.text:
• Arrived at Silver Mist Lodge with a satchel, tried to flee when he saw the party
  • Confessed to being hired to destroy the fireworks warehouse
  • Revealed the Yeshou family as the ones who paid him
  • Disclosed his father's plan to leave Willowshore
  • Asked by the party to check if other kids were hired for similar pranks
  • Received the full 100 gold payment, escorted safely to Yong's forge by the party
  • Helped Yong at the forge while the party headed north

docs.title: Session Three (2026-02-12)
docs.text:
• Visited by Da Baishan and Boone in the evening at the forge
  • Reported that none of his friends were hired for sabotage—all are excited about the festival
  • Confirmed he asked them directly about "pranks" and payments from the Yeshou family; all said no
  • Was intimidated one final time by Da Baishan (Intimidation 23)—stepped back with wide eyes and a quivering voice, but stuck to his story
  • Boone clapped him on the shoulder reassuringly; Hong flinched and scampered off to "help Dad clean up"

docs.title: Session Four (2026-02-26)
docs.text:
• Fell into an old dry well trying to retrieve Kimmy's broken festival lantern—her "first wish" lantern for the river ceremony
  • Suffered a gash on his leg from a ceremonial dagger buried in the mud
  • Was too embarrassed to tell his father; sent Kimmy to find Boone instead
  • Rescued by Da Baishan, who climbed down and tied a rope around him
  • Blushed visibly through his kitsune fur when Da Baishan suggested he needed "a kiss to feel better"—Kimmy obliged with a peck on the cheek
  • The broken lantern meant Kimmy couldn't make her wish at the festival

docs.title: Session Fourteen (2026-08-20)
docs.text:
• Left home. The party returned to Willowshore to find Hong and Yong in a full public feud — Hong blaming his father, Yong blaming Hong, neither being discreet about it. Hong shouldered a packed bag and walked south alone, toward the inn or out of town entirely, while his father shouted good riddance behind him
  • This is the memory curse at its cruelest: the father and son who had planned to leave Willowshore together — bonded by the rescue, the windfall, and the dream of open coastlines — can now recall only their grudges. The GM confirmed those who interacted most with the party took the strongest dose, and "Yong and Hong had the most passionate reaction"
  • The townsfolk watched the argument, mumbled, and went back to work; no one consoled either of them
  • The cure exists — the remaining half of the Grandmother's seed, or the town-spirit path — but supply is short and Hong is walking

docs.title: Session Sixteen (2026-09-17)
docs.text:
• He didn't get far — and he came back. When Old Amber consumed the seed and the curse lifted from the whole town, the first thing the party saw outside Dew Drop Petals was Hong and Yong embracing in the square. Father and son remember the fight; neither feels it anymore
  • Came with his father to thank the party in the street, and stood by as Yong apologized for staying silent at the trial

docs.title: Kimmy
docs.text: The girl who ran across town to find a hero for a boy in a well.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Kimmy Age ~10-12 years old Ancestry Human Occupation Child Location Willowshore

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Kimmy is a young human girl, roughly ten to twelve years old—the same girl Boone rescued from the burning warehouse in Session One. She is brave enough to sprint across town to find help, and honest enough that her panic reads as genuine rather than performative.

Her family runs the Cloud Paper Lodge, a paper lantern shop whose fireworks were stored in the destroyed warehouse.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Kimmy is earnest and resourceful for her age. When Hong fell into the well, she didn't panic uselessly—she ran to find the one person she trusted to help: Boone, the dwarf who had already saved her once. She is loyal to Hong and clearly cares about him, though neither child seems ready to fully acknowledge what that means.

docs.title: Boone
docs.text: Kimmy trusts Boone implicitly after he rescued her from the warehouse fire. She sought him out by name when Hong needed help.

docs.title: Hong
docs.text: Hong and Kimmy are close friends with hints of a childhood crush. Hong broke her festival lantern—her "first wish" lantern for the river ceremony—while trying to retrieve it from the well for her. When Da Baishan suggested Hong needed "a kiss to feel better," Kimmy gave him a shy peck on the cheek.

docs.title: Session One (2026-01-30)
docs.text:
• Trapped in the burning warehouse with Hong
  • Rescued by Boone, who crashed through a window to deliver her to her mother

docs.title: Session Four (2026-02-26)
docs.text:
• Ran across town to find Boone, reporting that Hong had fallen into a well
  • Led Boone, Da Baishan, and Littlefinger to the old dry well
  • Hugged Hong with relief when he was pulled out
  • Kissed Hong on the cheek at Da Baishan's suggestion
  • Could not make her "first wish" at the festival because Hong had broken her lantern

docs.title: Kuji Yasho
docs.text: "Come, come. We have these smuggling tunnels all over the town. It's come in very handy in the past."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Kuji Yasho Ancestry Human Affiliation Yeshou family — son of Mido Location Willowshore and its surrounding hideouts

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Kuji is one of Mido's children — present in the background of the family's appearances throughout the campaign, but never previously named. He had appeared as a quiet figure beside his mother in the Yeshou estate, the festival, and Silver Mist Lodge.

He came forward into the light in Session Nine when he climbed up through the floor of a Willowshore warehouse — through one of the family's old smuggling tunnels — to extract the imprisoned party.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
What the party has seen of Kuji so far is calm, competent, and unsurprised. He moves through the family's tunnel network with the easy confidence of someone who has done it many times — apologizing once for the narrow squeeze near the entrance, but otherwise treating the operation like a routine extraction.

He shares his mother's pragmatism. He does not posture or boast. When greeted with surprise that the family had a tunnel under the warehouse, he answered simply: "It's come in very handy in the past."

docs.title: Skills & Notes
docs.text:
• Knows the tunnel network well — led the party through a route that opened from the warehouse floor, descended into a natural passage, ran past the chasm crevice, and surfaced in a hidden cave outcropping west of town
  • Trusted operative — sent ahead alone by Mido to retrieve the party, with prearranged extraction at the cave mouth
  • Logistics & quartermastering — at the end of the meeting, dispatched to retrieve gear from the family's stashes (full plate, healer's kits, sling, healing potions) and returned with most of what the party requested

docs.title: Mido
docs.text: His mother. He defers to her, but acts on his own judgment in the field — he was the one who decided exactly when and how to extract the party, on his own initiative.

docs.title: The Yeshou Family
docs.text: Born into it. The family's tunnel network and arms caches appear to be his particular domain. Da Baishan's quip — "I see it runs in the family" — was met by Kuji with the small, knowing smile of someone who has heard it before.

docs.title: The Party
docs.text: Sees them as allies of the family in a difficult moment. Treated them efficiently, without flattery, and was willing to scrounge specific gear for them on short notice — including a heavy plate sized for Boone.

docs.title: Earlier sessions
docs.text:
• Present in the background as one of Mido's children at the Yeshou estate, the Festival of Returning Spirits, and Silver Mist Lodge
  • Unnamed in the party's records until Session Nine

docs.title: Session Nine (2026-05-07)
docs.text:
• Climbed up through a hidden floor-hatch in the warehouse where the party was confined; revealed the family's network of smuggling tunnels beneath Willowshore
  • Led the party through the tunnels — partially exposed at one point to the chasm crevice — to a hidden cave mouth at an outcropping west of town, where Mido waited in a rickshaw with the family's surviving guard
  • Dispatched mid-meeting to retrieve gear from the family's stashes; returned with two healer's toolkits, a sized full plate for Boone, a sling for Littlefinger, and five potions of healing
  • Mido named the family's intent to keep using "spy and other smuggling tunnels" to monitor Kurosawa once the party departed; Kuji is the most likely operator of that network

docs.title: Liwen
docs.text: A florist who counts petals and keeps her opinions to herself.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Liwen Ancestry Human Occupation Florist Location Willowshore

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Liwen is a middle-aged woman in her forties, with long hair streaked with gray and permanently dirt-stained fingertips from years of gardening. She runs a tiny shop in Willowshore—barely more than a cart—selling flowers, arrangements, and whatever she can grow or gather. She supplies Radiant Willow with flowers for Dew Drop Petals.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Liwen is a private, cautious person who keeps her opinions close. She does not gossip freely and tends to avoid discussing the oni or the political changes in town. This is not deception but self-preservation—she has lived in Willowshore for years, likes the way things are, and fears what the new leadership might change.

She trusts Donkey, who is one of her regular herb suppliers, and is more forthcoming with him than she might be with strangers.

docs.title: Views on the Oni
docs.text: Liwen is quietly worried about the transition of power. She doesn't believe the change will be for the better, but keeps these thoughts to herself. She fulfilled Magistrate Kurosawa's order without complaint and did not volunteer information about it—though she shared the details when Donkey asked directly.

docs.title: The Lily Order
docs.text:
Magistrate Kurosawa personally visited Liwen and ordered five dozen white lilies—sixty flowers traditionally associated with funerals. When she asked the purpose, he said only that it was "an oni custom" and declined to elaborate. The specific quantity (five dozen) echoes the recurring pattern of fives connected to the ley lines and the ritual.

Liwen found the order unusual and mentioned it to Radiant Willow. She fulfilled it, delivered the lilies to the magistrate, and chose not to ask further questions.

docs.title: Donkey
docs.text: Liwen and Donkey have a regular supplier relationship. He brings her herbs and new plant specimens from his foraging trips, and she trusts his judgment on botanical matters. She was forthcoming with him about the lily order when he visited.

docs.title: Radiant Willow
docs.text: Willow is one of Liwen's primary customers, purchasing flowers for Dew Drop Petals.

docs.title: Session Four (2026-02-26)
docs.text:
• Visited by Donkey at her shop; discussed business and the festival preparations
  • Revealed that Magistrate Kurosawa ordered five dozen white lilies (funeral flowers), claiming it was an "oni custom"
  • Expressed cautious worry about the change in leadership
  • Asked Donkey to bring back new buds from his next foraging trip

docs.title: Session Eleven (2026-06-04)
docs.text: • Appeared in the memory-corruption vision the party witnessed in the Hollow of Seven Cedars pool — shown looking at the party without recognition, one of the projected effects of Kurosawa's Root rite flowing into Willowshore. (A vision of a possible future, not a confirmed present.)

docs.title: Luda
docs.text: "I don't trust any of those demons as far as I could toss them."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Luda Ancestry Human (elderly) Occupation Seamstress, herbalist, informal arcane supplier Location Luda's Shop, Willowshore

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Luda is an older woman who runs a modest shop in Willowshore. Her official trade is seamstress work—clothing repair, fabric, patches, general goods—but she also deals in rare plants, mushrooms, and alchemical ingredients. She has enough knowledge of alchemy and arcane components to supply spell-casters with the specialized inks, powders, and botanical materials needed for scrolls, spell transcription, and other magical crafting.

She is not a wizard or a practitioner, but she knows what the practitioners need and where to find it.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Luda is blunt, suspicious of authority, and unapologetically hostile toward the oni presence in Willowshore. She does not mince words or soften her opinions. She views the entire oni regime as corrupt and self-serving.

docs.title: Donkey
docs.text: Luda is one of Donkey's regular suppliers for spell components—special inks, crushed fungi, and other arcane crafting materials. They have a transactional but trusting relationship. When Donkey asked her to report on Kurosawa's future purchases, she agreed without hesitation.

docs.title: Magistrate Kurosawa
docs.text: Kurosawa demanded arcane ingredients from Luda in high volume with extreme specificity. He paid her, but the interaction was cold and intimidating. She is deeply concerned about the purpose of the ingredients and considers the oni's presence in Willowshore a facade for something sinister.

docs.title: Notable Quotes
docs.text:
"I don't trust any of those demons as far as I could toss them."

"They all are up to no good. There's something going on and I do not believe it's in any of our interests."

docs.title: Session Five (2026-03-12)
docs.text:
• Introduced as Donkey's regular supplier for arcane crafting components
  • Revealed that Magistrate Kurosawa demanded high-volume, highly specific arcane ingredients from her—she was compensated but disturbed by the cold interaction and the nature of the request
  • Believes the oni presence is a facade for a nefarious arcane purpose
  • Holds an extremely low opinion of all the oni, especially Kurosawa
  • Agreed to track and report any future purchases by the magistrate to Donkey

docs.title: Session Eight (2026-04-22)
docs.text:
• Called as a prosecution witness during the Rite of Open Reckoning—visibly reluctant to testify at all
  • Admitted under Kurosawa's questioning that she had never trusted him personally
  • Kurosawa then turned the questioning: Luda confirmed that Donkey had asked her to spy on the magistrate and report his purchases; she said she "didn't feel she had a choice"
  • Refused to condemn the party outright: "I don't think they can be seen as deceiving." — not a defense, but not the condemnation Kurosawa was hoping for either
  • Her testimony was the most awkward for both sides: it damaged both the magistrate's impartiality and the party's deniability about surveilling him

docs.title: Session Fifteen (2026-09-03)
docs.text:
• Met Donkey at her door with a scowl and a ledger: "I think you still owe me seven gold pieces" (the true figure may have been four; she stood at seven; he paid). "Excellent. The counts are settled. How can I help you today?"
  • Supplied the Land of Dreams expedition: three doses of nightshade and pressed poppy petals for 9 gold — cut with the proper instruments, prepared in her back room in fifteen minutes, potency preserved. She knew exactly what the brew was for and asked no questions beyond "how many doses?"
  • Handled the transaction with professional discretion: "Please don't loiter around and look obvious"
  • Sent Donkey off with the campaign's most on-brand herbalist blessing: "Thank you, my old friend — and I hope you have powerful dreams"
  • Was pickpocketed for 6 of the 9 gold by Littlefinger on the way out (a 29; she didn't notice). The party's net cost for the entire expedition: three gold

docs.title: Magistrate Kurosawa
docs.text: "I could make people do things. That's not what I want to do here."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Name Kurosawa Title Magistrate Ancestry Oni Affiliation Shogun Tsuneni's regime Location Willowshore (temporarily at the Yeshou estate)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Magistrate Kurosawa is a 7-foot-tall oni with striking blue skin and a fierce, commanding presence. He wears samurai-style lamellar armor and carries an enormous nodachi—a massive two-handed katana that most humans couldn't even lift. His very presence seems to command attention; he rarely needs to raise his voice.

He arrived in Willowshore a few days before Mayor Masru, taking up residence in the Yeshou family estate after displacing them. His stated purpose is to ensure the transfer of power proceeds smoothly.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Kurosawa projects extreme confidence bordering on arrogance—the certainty of someone who knows they hold all the power. Yet he is not simply a brute. He understands the value of diplomacy and soft power, preferring persuasion to force when possible.

He views the party as useful tools: outsiders without entrenched loyalties who can investigate without raising suspicions. He is direct about this arrangement—he does not pretend to be their friend.

"I could make people do things. That's not what I want to do here."

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Establish oni authority over Willowshore with minimal resistance
  • Identify and neutralize potential sources of dissent—currently suspects the party
  • The Confluence (the Five Keys) — A multi-site geomantic ritual to harmonize five ley-line "veins" (Willow, Root, Stone, Water, Ash) so the Mother of a Thousand Wings resonance passes through Willowshore and transforms the city into a chrysalis (see the recovered note)
  • The Gosembiki — The first device, "the star beneath Gosembiki," is awakened (Session 7–8)
  • The Mourndusk Willow ritual — Earlier summoning groundwork at the ancient tree in the Dark Woods
  • A device — Commissioned Yong to build the apparatus; the recovered note confirms multiple devices in series, one per key
  • Arcane stockpiling — Purchasing high-volume, specific arcane ingredients from Luda, a local alchemical supplier

docs.title: The Note of Five Keys
docs.text:
A planning note in Kurosawa's own hand, signed — Kurosawa and recovered by Littlefinger from the graveyard wall crevice in Session Nine. It is the single most damning piece of physical evidence the party has ever held against him.

Excerpts:

"The confluence is upon us. Five veins. Five keys. Willow. Root. Stone. Water. Ash. Each must be forced into accord. Each must be corrected. Each must sing the same note."

"The first device has awakened the star beneath Gosembiki. Four remain."

"The old lovers' grove, now called the Hollow of Seven Cedars, must be opened at the root next. Memory can be cut, grafted, and made to grow in a new direction."

"Cloudbreaker Cairn must be made to bow. Even stone yields when proper law is spoken with sufficient force."

"The drowned markers of the River's Lantern Spine must be turned with the current. Water carries every name."

"The Terrace of Whispering Clay must be sealed last. Clay receives the hand. Clay remembers the shape."

"When all five lines flow as one, the Mother's resonance will pass through Willowshore. Not death. Not ruin. Transformation. The city will become chrysalis. Its history will soften. Its old loyalties will dissolve."

"Let the weak call it corruption. Let the sentimental call it loss. When the lines are harmonized, the Mother's reign begins."

"And if I must die beneath her wings, then I will at least die moving the world."

Key Site Action Status Willow Gosembiki ruins "Awakened the star" Done (Session 7–8) — though the device was pulled, not seated as planned Root Hollow of Seven Cedars (Lovers' Grove) "Opened at the root" — memory cut, grafted, regrown Done — and witnessed (Session 11). Grafted months ago; party arrived to a fully corrupted grove and tore out the master graft Stone Cloudbreaker Cairn "Made to bow" — proper law spoken with sufficient force Pending Water River's Lantern Spine "Turned with the current" — drowned markers realigned Pending Ash Terrace of Whispering Clay "Sealed last" — clay holds the new shape Final

The note frames Willowshore as a chrysalis, not a target — the city's history softens, its loyalties dissolve, and what emerges is the dominion of the Mother. Kurosawa is also explicit that he expects to die in the doing of it.

docs.title: The Party
docs.text: Kurosawa recruited the party as his deputies, paying them 50 gold up front with 50 more promised upon successful completion of their duties. He sees them as expendable assets who can do the groundwork he cannot—moving among the common folk without inspiring the same fear and silence that follows him.

docs.title: The Yeshou Family
docs.text: He views the Willowshore Ruling Family as the most obvious threat to a smooth transition. He displaced them from their estate and suggested the party investigate them first.

docs.title: Mayor Masru
docs.text: Kurosawa serves as the advance guard for the incoming mayor. His role is to prepare Willowshore for the transfer of power.

docs.title: Notable Quotes
docs.text:
"This explosion the day before our arrival is highly suspect."

"I need some deputies, some eyes on the ground, some folks who will... that I can hold accountable."

"Be careful what you wish for." — On the consequences of failure

docs.title: Kurosawa's Error
docs.text:
The Order of the Palatine Eye's Book of Divided Testimony opened to Boone's hand in Session Ten. The second of two truths it revealed names Kurosawa's mistake outright:

A tyrant believes law can replace loyalty.

A geomancer believes lines can replace roots.

Both are wrong until the roots are made to forget themselves.

The Order's reading is theoretical and devastating. Geomancy alone is insufficient to invoke the Mother of a Thousand Wings — the Confluence rite described in the note cannot harmonize five ley-line keys into the Mother's resonance unless the roots themselves forget what they are.

That is precisely what the second key — Root — is for. The Hollow of Seven Cedars is not just one site of five; it is the conditional joint of the entire ritual.
